title: Metrics and KPIs: definition, target, owner and frequency

videos.script: Caio asks for one number. The on-time delivery rate, every Monday. {{ask}} It sounds like a simple request, and it is not. Lívia takes one week of deliveries from the warehouse. Fourteen orders. She finds three honest answers. Eighty-three percent. Seventy-one. Fifty. {{three}} Nobody made a mistake. Each person counted a different thing and called it on time. This lesson is about the work that stops that happening. {{metric}} First, the difference between a metric and a KPI. Every KPI is a metric, and very few metrics are KPIs. {{card}} Then the card. Eleven fields written down before anybody computes the number: what is counted, what is left out, who owns it, how often, and when somebody must act. {{tree}} Then leading and lagging indicators, and a tree that rebuilds online sales from visits, conversion and the average ticket. It shows how a campaign can raise visits by a quarter and leave sales exactly where they were. {{target}} Last, the target. Where it comes from, why it is two numbers, and the ways it gets met without anything getting better.
